objective: Open time integration as a research family on the step-size-resolution closure line, reproducing the paper's own cases, and measure the lab's own exposure first: every unsteady result the lab has ever shipped ran on a first-order time scheme and no second-order time scheme is in service anywhere
rationale: Two things make this item unusually well posed. The first is that the source is in the house and its temporal half is explicit: the closure matches the local truncation error of a batch of fine implicit-explicit multistep steps against one coarse step, corrects it with a closed-form additive term plus a small learned surrogate for the terms that are not free at inference, and prints the expansion whose leading terms scale with the third and fourth powers of the coarse step, with the reproduction cases named as decaying two-dimensional turbulence on a 256 by 256 grid to a horizon of 60, flow past a cylinder, and a cape case whose panel the paper itself marks as still to be added. The claim to reproduce is stated sharply enough to fail: the corrected coarse-step scheme should behave like the same scheme at a fraction of the step, at a fraction of the runtime. The second is that the lab's own exposure was never measured and is larger than anyone has said. A sweep of the lab's own dictionaries and workflow code finds the steady cases on a steady-state time derivative, as expected, and every unsteady case on first-order Euler, with the second-order backward and Crank-Nicolson schemes appearing nowhere in the lab's own code or dictionaries at all. So every unsteady statistic the lab has shipped, including its shedding results, carries first-order temporal truncation that has never been quantified. The one time-step sensitivity study on the record is a single case where halving the Courant limit moved the cycle mean by 1.8e-5 and the phase-aligned waveform by 1.4e-3 of the cycle band, against a spatial channel worth about 20 percent on the same case, so the lab has exactly one data point saying the temporal channel is small there and no data point anywhere else. That asymmetry is the cheapest thing this family can fix first. Axis A: reading-kind, with the first rung spending nothing and the second priced from the one measured time-step arm the lab has. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.

cost_basis: measured on the lab's only time-step arm: the valve case re-solved its final cycle at half the Courant limit in 413 seconds of wall on the same mesh, and the second rung here is that same class of work, one existing unsteady case re-solved under a second-order time scheme against its first-order twin; the unsteady cylinder family also carries a fitted per-family cost law from 417 ledger rows with a holdout median error of 1.9 percent, and that fit is the cross-check on the 30 core-min figure rather than its source
expected_knowledge_gain: Two rungs, four outcomes. Rung one spends nothing and answers a question the lab has never asked: how large is the first-order temporal truncation on the unsteady results already shipped. If it is negligible everywhere, the lab has a defensible statement it currently cannot make; if it is not, one or more shipped unsteady statistics need a caveat and that is a correction, not a nuisance. Rung two either reproduces the paper's stated scaling for the corrected scheme, which converts somebody else's research into lab capability with a graded reproduction behind it, or fails to, which is a reproduction result worth recording either way and is the whole point of the reproduction-first framing. The by-product in both cases is a second-order time scheme in service, which the lab does not have today.
sequencing: Rung one is dispatchable now and spends nothing. Rung two is slow-burn family work under strategy rule 4 and queues behind Ladder V under rule 1.
gate: STRATEGY PROOF CLAUSE, verbatim: 'Time integration: her step-size-resolution closure line enters the lab as a research family (LMM->RK order elevation), with the lab reproducing the paper's cases. Sanaa's own research becomes lab capability.' Operationalised in three parts. (a) An exposure audit, at zero compute, stating for every unsteady result the lab has published which time scheme it ran, what order that scheme is, and whether a time-step sensitivity number exists for it; the audit fails if any shipped unsteady statistic is left with no answer. (b) A reproduction of the paper's named cases, decaying two-dimensional turbulence first, graded against the printed scaling of the truncation-error expansion, with the grading criterion written before the reproduction runs and the cape case excluded because the paper itself has not done it. (c) A second-order time scheme brought into service on one existing unsteady case with the first-order twin as its control, and the shift reported. A reproduction that grades itself against its own output rather than against the printed expansion fails part (b).
